newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran urges joint security steps with Arab neighbours.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges joint security steps with Arab neighbours.

text.p: Iran has called on its Arab neighbours in the Gulf to take steps towards joint security arrangements with the Islamic republic to guarantee peace in the oil-rich region, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.

It quoted a Foreign Ministry statement as saying late on Tuesday that a summit communique by leaders from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates on Monday criticising Iran only served Western and Israeli interests.

"The Islamic republic of Iran once more stresses that it does not pose any threat to any neighbours in the region and further it invites (the Gulf Arab states) to take an initiative in bringing about a joint security arrangement of the nations in the region to guarantee stability, regional security and help the Islamic republic of Iran safeguard its vast territorial waters...in the interest of all," the ministry said.
It also asked its Arab neighbours "to take steps in the direction of Islamic solidarity and good neighbourly ties instead of sparking instigations."

Leaders of five of the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries on Monday criticised Iran's military development programmes and deployment of surface-to-surface missiles in the region which they said exceeded "conventional" defensive needs and urged international agencies to rid the area of all weapons of mass destruction.
The sixth GCC state, Bahrain, boycotted the group's annual summit over a border dispute with host Qatar. Earlier this year Bahrain accused Iran of plotting to overthrow its government.

Gulf Arab states had repeatedly accused Iran of posing a threat to the security of the region -- which has about half the world's proven oil reserves -- and accused it of interfering in the internal affairs of the region's countries.

"It is astounding that the Persian Gulf states who have triggered an arms race in the region by contracting huge weapons deals with arrogant powers and by building military bases on their soil, want Iran which has a legitimate right to guarantee security in the Persian Gulf as an important international waterway, to ignore its own national security," the Iranian statement said.

It reiterated its willingness to hold bilateral talks with the United Arab Emirates to settle a row over three strategic Gulf islands claimed by both countries. But it also reiterated its stance that it had total sovereignty over the islands.
